weather.tip: 86% chance of rain today — carry an umbrella on your commute and budget extra time if showers hit during rush hour; ORR and other flood-prone stretches slow down fastest once the rain starts.

around.headline: Doctors urge Bengaluru parents to keep sick children home as H1N1 cases rise
around.summary: With flu-like illness already forcing one school to shut this week over an H1N1 outbreak, doctors are now urging parents citywide to keep children with fever or cough home rather than send them to school. If your child shows flu symptoms, keep them home until fever-free for a full 24 hours instead of waiting for a school notice.

around.headline: Bengaluru math teacher accused of beating a student with a stick
around.summary: A math teacher in Bengaluru is facing allegations of beating a student with a stick, reviving concern over corporal punishment in schools despite it being banned under the RTE Act. If your child mentions being hit or shows marks, document it and put a written complaint to the school the same day.

around.headline: ORR morning jams stretch 13.5 km as firms push back on mandatory WFH plan
around.summary: Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road saw rush-hour jams stretch 13.5 km today, as tech firms wrote to the GBA opposing a proposed mandatory work-from-home order tied to the road's Rs 450-crore white-topping work — arguing the city should prioritise Metro capacity instead. If you commute the ORR, expect the congestion to continue with no WFH mandate yet in place.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Indian Express, Moneycontrol

around.headline: Metro Blue Line Phase 2A trials expected from October; Hebbal–airport link unlikely before mid-2027
around.summary: Trial runs on the Blue Line's Phase 2A stretch should begin in October, but the Hebbal-to-airport link is unlikely to be ready by June 2027 as work beyond Yelahanka lags. Don't plan an airport Metro commute around this stretch any time soon.

around.headline: GBA sets August 30 deadline to clear footpath encroachments; repeat offenders face double penalty
around.summary: Bengaluru's civic minister has directed the GBA to clear footpath encroachments and waste by August-end, and repeat encroachers will now face double the usual penalty. If a footpath near you is blocked, this is the window to flag it to your ward office.
around.source: India Today, The Hindu, The New Indian Express

around.headline: 7 private medical facilities fined for KPME violations in Bengaluru, 3 lose licences
around.summary: Health authorities fined seven private medical facilities for violating the Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, and three had their licences revoked. Before choosing a clinic or diagnostic centre, it's worth checking it's properly KPME-registered.

around.headline: Supreme Court says NTA needs to be institutionalised, tech reforms needed after NEET paper-leak concerns
around.summary: The Supreme Court said India's National Testing Agency needs a stronger institutional structure and technology safeguards in the wake of NEET paper-leak concerns. For Bengaluru's large pool of NEET aspirants and their families, this signals changes are likely to how the medical entrance exam is run in coming cycles.

street_smart.title: You pick your child up from school and notice red marks on their arm. They tell you their math teacher hit them with a stick for getting sums wrong — the same day news breaks of a Bengaluru math teacher accused of exactly that. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a Bengaluru math teacher is accused of beating up a student with a stick (The Times of India). Corporal punishment as a street-smart topic hasn't appeared in the last three weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: It's evening, your child is otherwise fine but visibly upset and has faint red marks from the stick. The school hasn't sent any communication about the incident.

choices.text: Write down what your child told you with the date and time, photograph the marks, and submit a written complaint to the school principal and the School Development & Monitoring Committee the same day — escalate to Childline (1098) or the district Child Welfare Committee if the school doesn't respond.
choices.feedback: Correct. Corporal punishment is banned under Section 17 of the RTE Act, but schools that get only a quiet, verbal complaint often let it slide. A same-day written record with photos is what actually forces a response, and it's the paper trail you'd need if this ever has to go further.

choices.text: Tell your child to 'be more careful next time' and not upset the teacher again — a bit of strictness never hurt anyone.
choices.feedback: This is exactly how cases like today's keep happening: when it isn't reported, the same teacher does it again to other children too. Corporal punishment isn't 'strictness' — it's illegal, and treating it as normal is what lets it continue unchecked.

choices.text: Show up at school the next morning and confront the teacher loudly in front of the class or other parents.
choices.feedback: Without anything on record, a shouting match becomes your word against theirs, and the school can simply deny it happened. It also risks getting you dismissed as 'the difficult parent' instead of getting the incident formally investigated — document first, then escalate in writing.

choices.text: Skip the school entirely and go straight to the police to file a complaint against the teacher.
choices.feedback: For a real physical injury this route is valid, but going only to the police means the school itself is never compelled to review its own oversight, and there's no institutional record backing you if the case needs it. For serious harm, do both — a written complaint to the school and a police complaint — not one instead of the other.

takeaways: Corporal punishment is banned nationwide under Section 17 of the RTE Act, 2009 — no school can wave it off as discipline.
Document first: photograph any injury and write down your child's account with date and time, before you approach anyone.
Escalation ladder: school principal/SDMC in writing, then Childline 1098 or the district Child Welfare Committee if there's no response, and police for serious physical harm.

quiz.question: What illness prompted Bengaluru doctors today to urge parents to keep sick children home from school?
quiz.why: Cases have been rising citywide since this week's school outbreak, and doctors are now treating it as an active seasonal wave rather than an isolated case.

quiz.question: By when has Bengaluru's GBA been directed to clear footpath encroachments across the city?
quiz.why: Repeat encroachers will now face double the usual penalty as a further deterrent.

quiz.question: According to Deccan Herald, how long did Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road morning traffic jam stretch today?
quiz.why: It's part of why tech firms are opposing a mandatory work-from-home order tied to the road's Rs 450-crore white-topping project, pushing instead to prioritise Metro capacity.

quiz.question: Under India's Right to Education Act, corporal punishment in schools is:
options: Left to each state to decide
quiz.why: Section 17 of the RTE Act, 2009 bans both physical punishment and mental harassment of a child, and makes school staff liable for action if they violate it.

quiz.question: What is India's unified emergency helpline number that connects to police, fire and ambulance?
quiz.why: 112 was rolled out nationally to replace the separate 100 (police), 101 (fire) and 102 (ambulance) numbers with a single number routed to the nearest responder.
